title: Canonical identity-open underived restriction and section arrow
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For every scheme $T$, use its pulled-back coefficient ring $\Lambda_T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and internal module category $\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the module inverse and direct images and their specified adjunctions [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. For arbitrary schemes $U,D,Z$, arrows $j:U\to Z$, $i:U\to D$ and $h:D\to Z$, and an equality $h\circ i=j$, define $c_h:j^*h_*\to i^*$ to be the canonical underived commutative-square restriction mate [def-sfb-open-square-restriction-mates] for the square with top arrow $i$, left arrow $\operatorname{id}_U$, right arrow $h$ and bottom arrow $j$, followed by the canonical identification $(\operatorname{id}_U)_*i^*\cong i^*$. This identity direct-image identification is the sectionwise identity comparison of the published module direct images. If $j$ and $i$ are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], then for each object $V\xrightarrow{v}U$ of the small pro-etale site define $e_{h,V}:(V\xrightarrow{i\circ v}D)\to h^{-1}(V\xrightarrow{j\circ v}Z)$ to be the site morphism whose underlying scheme map is the pullback lift $V\to V\times_ZD$ with projections $\operatorname{id}_V$ and $i\circ v$. These are specified constructions with the canonical coefficient actions; no Cartesian, identity-locus, quasi-compactness, finite-type, admissibility or invertibility hypothesis is imposed on $c_h$, and no invertibility assertion for either map is made.
